parsed.explanation: No documented trans-presentation convictions and prosecutions are described as limited, which keeps this above the severe-criminalisation anchors. However the same-sex statute is documented as an active police lever: systematic harassment, arbitrary detention, extortion, assault, complaints ignored and forced examinations condemned as torture, with police acknowledged as foremost perpetrators. Gender expression is also targeted via vagrancy/personation provisions, and birth-sex custody is the practical default with only a discretionary, locally-issued-ID exception a visitor cannot use. No operative anti-discrimination recourse offsets this. Combined regime is therefore high-risk, near 0.35-C/0.25-A.

entry_documents.exposure: Same-sex provisions structure policing; foreign-document acceptance and border questioning of trans visitors not documented. Vagrancy/personation provisions could be used on document/presentation mismatch.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. Local gender-recognition card from 2016 is resident-facing and does not establish foreign-passport acceptance.
entry_documents.interaction: Document or presentation mismatch could move a visitor into the documented police harassment/extortion system with no documented border remedy.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police documented using threat of arrest to assault, harass and extort LGBTQIA people; arbitrary detention and forced anal/vaginal examinations described as torture. No dedicated trans prison housing; birth-sex default.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Holders of local recognised ID may be placed by preferred gender where possible, others by doctor assessment; visitor cannot obtain this route. No statutory placement rule.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Investigation under Sections 365/365A leads to detention where birth-sex placement, medicalised discretion and official fear of trans identification govern custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No national bathroom or public-facility rule documented; birth-sex ward system extends to prisons and, by system, facilities. No subnational variation documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private/commercial facility access not documented. No anti-discrimination protection covering sexual orientation or gender identity to support access.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Absence of a documented universal facility ban does not offset custody placement, which is the documented universal exposure if detained.

care_services.exposure: Patients report ignorance, curiosity and ridicule from medical staff; hormone therapy described as fraught; surgery relatively inaccessible. Blood service bars MSM donors.
care_services.protection: No surgical requirement for local certification. Emergency ward placement and visitor medication access not documented.
care_services.interaction: If injured or detained, a visitor may encounter the same medical ignorance and birth-sex placement system, increasing outing and misplacement risk.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Sections 365/365A carry up to 10 years, 10-20 if victim under 16; prosecutions limited and no convictions found in 2012, but law brands LGBTQ people as criminals and enables moral policing and extortion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Head of state in 2021 affirmed dignity regardless of sexuality/gender; psychiatrists called for decriminalisation. No repeal or operative protection documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Limited formal prosecution coexists with efficient informal enforcement by police, so functioning institutions are the exposure, not recourse.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No youth-specific care, travel, or guardian findings in dossier.
minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented. The under-16 penalty enhancement relates to offences against a minor, not to a trans minor travelling or an adult guardian.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Advocacy and human-rights reports document police ignoring LGBTQ complaints, especially sexual violence/blackmail, and police themselves assaulting/harassing/extorting. No trans-specific violence rate documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented. No anti-discrimination law; police and the national human rights commission acknowledged police as foremost perpetrators before the 2023 piece.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A victim reporting street violence faces the documented perpetrator institution, with citing Section 365 as justification, making protection unavailable.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Remedies are weak: administrative circulars deemed insufficient without legal reform, conversion-therapy ban unsupported by 2024, no comprehensive protections. Current prosecution rate after 2012 unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Local certification exists since 2016 without surgery, but bureaucratic process may be onerous and is resident-facing, not a visitor remedy.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper/non-statutory circulation and a resident ID route do not remedy police extortion, forced examinations or birth-sex custody for a foreign visitor.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: police systematically stop, harass and extort gender-nonconforming people, complaints without discipline, no effective recourse. This dossier adds forced examinations and birth-sex custody and a 10-year statute, but lacks documented routine hotel/terminal stops of foreign travellers, so similar to slightly more severe than 0.35-C.

Similar tier: repeated police detention, extortion, birth-sex custody with abuse, treating complainants as offenders. This dossier is somewhat less severe because prosecutions are limited with no convictions documented in 2012 and no documented hotel raids, placing it above 0.25-A but below 0.35 in state coercion frequency.

Higher safety: 0.55-C has an unenforced same-sex law, no use against trans people, familiar gender-diverse roles and prosecuted assaults. Here the statute is actively used as a police lever, police are foremost perpetrators, and custody is birth-sex by default, so materially below 0.55-C.

Higher safety: 0.15-A has regular sweeps and repeated convictions with months imprisonment for presentation. Here formal prosecutions are limited/no convictions in 2012, so the documented sequence is extortion/abuse rather than near-routine imprisonment, keeping it above 0.15-A.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is one national system: a latent-but-leveraged criminal statute, police who extort and ignore victims, forced examinations, and birth-sex custody with only a local-ID discretionary exception. Resident LGR, mixed public opinion (72.5% against punishment, 69% against unions) and a 2021 dignity statement are climate signals, not visitor protections. The final operative interaction is outing/document mismatch -> police investigation -> detention by birth sex, with no documented remedy that changes outcomes. That places the case at the high-risk end of elevated risk, around 0.30.
